source: Authorized complete-film uploads from filmmaker John Valenti, Supreme and Dexlix Patinetas, supplemented by SkateVideoSite, Theories of Atlantis, We Are Skaters and Urbeskate

films.title: FREE TIME
films.description: John Valenti's 20-minute independent film crosses New York, Madrid, Barcelona, Lisbon and Tokyo through seven named chapter riders and two broad montages. Filmed from 2017 through 2024, the project gives Valenti the filming and editing credits while documenting 31 skating appearances.
creditNotes: John Valenti's authorized complete-film description identifies seven riders in named chapter positions and formally credits Valenti with filming and editing.

SkateVideoSite independently classifies FREE TIME as a 20-minute 2024 independent film by John Valenti, catalogs all 31 appearances, documents the five-city footprint and lists five additional production contributors.

Only riders explicitly named in the authorized chapter list are labeled as chapter riders. The remaining independently documented skaters are retained as montage or additional appearances, and generic production credits are not assigned narrower unsupported roles.
locations: New York City, New York, USA
films.locationNote: The filmmaker's description names New York, Madrid, Barcelona, Lisbon and Tokyo, and SkateVideoSite independently records the same five filming locations and four-country production footprint.
films.historicalContext: Filmed across five international cities from 2017 through 2024, FREE TIME is a seven-year independent project that pairs focused rider chapters with two travel-heavy montages and a deep cross-generational roster.
films.artworkNotes: The exact authorized upload's 1920x1080 YouTube artwork was visually reviewed on 2026-09-17. It is dedicated FREE TIME title artwork over a fisheye skate photograph, credits John Valenti on-image and carries no trailer, episode or compilation labeling.

sourceRecords.sourceDetails: John Valenti's own channel hosts the uninterrupted complete film and publishes its chapter, filmmaker and location credits. YouTube reports channelId UCA-Ph1eBnWW91O0am7rxKLQ, a 1,179-second feature, April 4, 2024 publication, OK playability and permitted embedding.
Theories of Atlantis carries a first-party release post for John Valenti's complete FREE TIME project.
Independent filmography classifies FREE TIME as a 20-minute 2024 John Valenti film, catalogs 31 skaters and five production contributors, and documents the five-city international production.

rights.basis: External embed of the uninterrupted complete film on filmmaker John Valenti's own channel; TrickBook does not download or rehost the film.

films.title: HEADBANGER
films.description: Supreme's 31-minute full-length, directed by William Strobeck, brings 30 skaters together across the brand's established roster and a younger wave of contributors. Strobeck also shares filming duties with Johnny Wilson, Alex Greenberg, Omar Massiah and Dan Lundy.
creditNotes: Supreme's official complete-film description names all 30 featured skaters, formally credits William Strobeck as director and identifies all five camera contributors.
SkateVideoSite independently classifies HEADBANGER as a 31-minute 2025 Supreme full-length by Strobeck, corroborates the 30-skater roster, camera credits and Miami location.
The official source does not publish a formal part hierarchy, so all 30 skaters are retained under the source's featured-rider label rather than being promoted to unsupported solo-part status.
films.locationNote: SkateVideoSite documents Miami as a filming location and the United States as the production country. No broader city list is inferred from the player.
films.historicalContext: HEADBANGER marked Supreme's return to a long-form team release after Play Dead and extended William Strobeck's decade-plus visual influence on the brand while foregrounding newer team faces alongside established riders.
films.artworkNotes: The exact official upload's 1920x1080 YouTube artwork was visually reviewed on 2026-09-17. It is dedicated HEADBANGER title artwork in pink over a film still and carries no trailer, episode or compilation labeling.

sourceRecords.sourceDetails: Supreme's official channel hosts the uninterrupted complete film and publishes its full featured-rider, director and camera credits. YouTube reports channelId UC0gPMaJlOsyuHiRywWn_tuQ, a 1,868-second feature, April 10, 2025 publication, OK playability and permitted embedding.

Independent filmography classifies HEADBANGER as a 31-minute 2025 Supreme full-length by William Strobeck, corroborates all 30 skaters and four additional camera credits, and records Miami as a location.
Contemporary independent skate coverage identifies HEADBANGER as Supreme's return to a long-form video after Play Dead and discusses Strobeck's influence and the arrival of newer team faces.

films.title: SUCUMBELE
films.description: Dexlix Patinetas' fourth full-length travels through several Mexican cities for 37 minutes, giving named sections to a 12-rider company lineup and documenting 21 additional friends and appearances. Teo Rojas and Enrique Alvarez lead the filmmaking credits, with Rojas also editing and contributing drone work to the production.
creditNotes: Dexlix Patinetas' official complete-film description identifies this as its fourth full video, names the 12 team and principal riders and says it was filmed across several Mexican cities.
Urbeskate independently corroborates the 12-rider company lineup, identifies Guillermo Martínez as the closing full part and distinguishes supporting appearances.

SkateVideoSite independently classifies SUCUMBELE as a 37-minute 2025 full-length by Teo Rojas and Enrique Alvarez, catalogs all 34 documented appearances and preserves the detailed production-credit list.

Only the official 12-rider lineup is labeled as team and named-section riders. The remaining catalogued skaters are retained as friends or additional appearances, and generic production credits are not assigned narrower roles.
films.locationNote: The official upload says the film was recorded in several Mexican cities. Urbeskate specifically documents Marcos Venegas skating transition in Baja California Sur; unsupported city names are not inferred.
films.historicalContext: SUCUMBELE is Dexlix Patinetas' fourth full video and a broad document of contemporary Mexican skateboarding, pairing the company's 12-rider core with a large friends section and Guillermo Martínez's independently documented closing part.
films.artworkNotes: The exact official upload's 1920x1080 YouTube artwork was visually reviewed on 2026-09-17. It is dedicated SUCUMBELE title artwork over a black-and-white skate photograph and carries no trailer, episode or compilation labeling.

sourceRecords.sourceDetails: Dexlix Patinetas' official channel hosts the uninterrupted fourth full video and publishes its 12-rider lineup and Mexican production context. YouTube reports channelId UC_iZcpc-kLKwrH78bfI3FJQ, a 2,226-second feature, May 22, 2025 publication, OK playability and permitted embedding.
Independent Mexican skate coverage corroborates the 12-rider Dexlix team lineup, supporting appearances, Baja California Sur context and Guillermo Martínez's closing part.

Independent filmography classifies SUCUMBELE as a 37-minute 2025 full-length by Teo Rojas and Enrique Alvarez, catalogs 34 skating appearances and preserves its soundtrack chapter and detailed production credits.
